title: Record ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
credits: Photos: Chris LeBoutillier, Anders Marlowe, Karthik B K / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: October has become the worst month yet for ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Washington Institute for Near East Policy counted twenty-eight attacks on ships in and around the strait this month, a record.
That makes one hundred and thirteen attacks since the US-Israeli war with Iran began, on the twenty-eighth of February.
The consultancy Marisks says a dozen ships were attacked in a single week, from the fifth to the eleventh of October, the most of the conflict.
A Reuters review of shipping data shows more than thirty giant crude tankers damaged since the war began, eleven of them in October.
Each of these supertankers can carry about two million barrels of oil.
Now, an oil spill has reached the beaches of Umm Al Quwain, in the United Arab Emirates.
The UAE's environment ministry says clean-up teams are at work, and the emirate's beaches have been closed.
Daily freight rates for tankers have topped one million dollars.
An analyst at the Washington Institute says Iran is stepping up attacks to keep pressure on energy markets, ahead of the US midterm elections in November.
For oil importers like Pakistan, every spike in tension can feed straight into fuel prices.
